prize_parts.citation: For the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles that encapsulate and deliver nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: I keep ionizable lipid nanoparticles as my single-part position after reading the full first round. Nothing said in round 1 touched the central scientific case: a pH-switchable lipid that is near neutral in circulation, binds and entraps nucleic acid at low pH, and turns cationic in the endosome to destabilise the membrane is a deliberate use of lipid self-assembly, phase behaviour and interfacial charge regulation, and the design variables (pKa, packing, helper lipid and PEG-lipid composition, mixing kinetics) are understood quantitatively. It is mature in the sense this committee should care about: an approved siRNA drug, billions of mRNA vaccine doses, and independent confirmation across many laboratories over three decades. The chair asks whether this is chemistry and not Medicine or formulation. I say it is chemistry because the achievement is a molecular design rule for a self-assembled particle, not the nucleic acid cargo; the 2023 Medicine prize recognised nucleoside modification and left the vehicle uncredited. The Vancouver trio of Cullis, Hope and Madden has the most coherent claim to the encapsulation concept, the ionizable cationic lipid idea and the scalable formulation process, and the citation is worded to that mechanism so that it does not cover lipidoid or polymer carriers as a whole.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the main weakness and I do not claim to have solved it. Anderson and Langer's lipidoid work and MacLachlan's translational formulation are substantial, and a three-person cut that leaves them out will be called narrow by some readers. The category risk is also real: a reader could treat this as enabling technology for the Medicine area. Finally, only I have this as a first preference and only Aili lists it as an alternative, so I cannot say the committee as a whole shares my weighting, and base editing has three explicit supporters. I should not mistake my own field's affinity for lipids for merit, and I treat that as a standing reason to hold this position with some humility.

responses.point: Brzezinski keeps base editing (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) first as the clearest attributable invention, with a stated deaminase mechanism and broad cross-member support, and names the 2020 CRISPR prize and the Kondo/Nishida question as risks.
responses.response: I agree that attribution is cleaner for base editing than for LNPs and that it is the most likely to gather a majority. I have moved it into my alternatives for that reason. I still do not rank it above B017, because the maturity gap runs the other way: base editing has first clinical use, while LNPs already underpin an approved drug and a vaccine platform at population scale. On the chair's increment question, I side with Chabes and Brzezinski that the 2020 prize honoured guided cleavage and not base conversion, so I do not treat it as disqualifying. But I note that the same logic applies to the 2023 prize and LNPs, and the committee should apply it evenly.

responses.point: Chabes argues that base editing is new chemistry, because the adenine editor needed an evolved TadA that has no natural DNA counterpart, and acknowledges that Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID leaves a fairness problem under a three-name cap.
responses.response: The TadA argument is persuasive to me as a chemistry argument and it is the strongest reason I now list B006 as an alternative. But the priority problem you raise for Kondo and Nishida is the same kind of problem I carry for Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan, and I think a committee that accepts a Liu-led trio for B006 despite Target-AID should find the Vancouver trio for B017 equally defensible, since in both cases the excluded work is parallel and not the originating concept. I also accept your earlier point that the ionizable-lipid and encapsulation concept sits in Vancouver, and I keep Cullis, Hope and Madden for that reason.

responses.point: Aili prefers degraders (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) as a single induced-proximity concept, with the approved cereblon glue lineage and clinical-stage degraders as evidence of maturity, and concedes that LNPs are further along on patient benefit.
responses.response: I accept that B068 is the broadest cross-member compromise and I keep it as an alternative. My concern remains that the citation joins two strands with different lineages: the engineered heterobifunctional degrader has no approval yet, and the glue mechanism was understood only after the drug was in use. If the committee wanted B068 I would ask for citation wording that names induced proximity and does not imply that PROTAC drugs are already on the market, and I would want Ciulli's ligand and ternary-complex work weighed against Handa for the third place. On your worry about the 2023 prize, I still think the overlap with LNPs is weak, since delivery was not what Karikó and Weissman were honoured for.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers biomolecular phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) as a physical-chemical organising principle of the cell.
responses.response: I share your enthusiasm for condensate thermodynamics, but after round 1 I have dropped B056 from my alternatives. The question the chair raised, whether in vivo condensates are genuine liquids and not gels, percolated networks or other assemblies, has not been answered, and Pappu and Mittag's role in the sequence-grammar theory makes a Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen trio contestable. I would be glad to see this recognised in a few years once the in vivo criteria are agreed, and I do not oppose it, but I cannot call it ready.

responses.point: Somfai prefers Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) as the cleanest synthetic method with two-person attribution, and notes the 2010 cross-coupling prize and Kosugi precedent.
responses.response: Your attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist and I do not dispute the mechanistic distinctness of C-N coupling. My reservation is the category balance you yourself raise: synthetic methodology has been recognised often, and the physical-chemical and materials side of the field has been recognised less. That is a consideration and not a decisive argument, and I would not oppose B032 on merit.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a Vancouver trio for LNPs without Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan, or regards the exclusion as making the candidacy unworkable.
Whether the 2023 Medicine prize makes a delivery prize read as a second award for the same medicines.
Whether base editing's short clinical record and the Target-AID priority question will be resolved enough to change my ranking of B006 relative to B017.
Whether an approved heterobifunctional degrader appears, which would raise my view of B068's maturity.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict. My research on lipid self-assembly overlaps in subject with lipid nanoparticles, but I have no known personal, collaborative or institutional connection to Cullis, Hope, Madden, Anderson, Langer or MacLachlan. I share Lund with Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai and overlap in field with Daniel Aili, which are connections among colleagues and not to any shortlisted candidate. I request no recusal.
